polls.note: Real Time Big Data, released on Sep 1 (Gazeta do Povo, CNN Brasil, Poder360, Money Times, R7, CartaCapital, VEJA, Brasil 247). ⚠️ THE POLLSTER PUBLISHED TWO FIRST-ROUND SCENARIOS AND THEY GIVE DIFFERENT NUMBERS FOR THE SECOND AND THIRD PLACES. With Pablo Marçal on the list, Lula 38%, Flávio Bolsonaro 29% and Augusto Cury 10%. Without Marçal, Lula 38%, Flávio 30% and Cury 11%. The day’s headlines circulated the second scenario without saying it was the one without Marçal, and that is why the panel carries both, labelled. In the runoff, Lula 44% x Flávio 44%, a tie. ⭐ IN THE SCENARIO AGAINST RONALDO CAIADO, LULA LOSES 45% TO 43%. Across the 41 runoff simulations in the panel’s base, Lula has trailed in four, and all four were against Flávio Bolsonaro. It is the first time in the base that a name other than him shows in front. In the others, Lula 43% x Romeu Zema 40%, Lula 44% x Renan Santos 37% and Lula 44% x Pablo Marçal 40%. In rejection, Lula and Flávio tie at 50%, Marçal has 48%, Renan 40%, Caiado 39%, Zema 36% and Augusto Cury 24%, the lowest among the seven names tested in this poll. Field Aug 27 to 31, n=2,000, margin of 2pp, 95% confidence, registration BR-03490/2026. ⭐ IT IS THE PANEL’S FIRST NATIONAL POLL WHOSE FIELD REACHES Aug 31, and therefore the first to cover the full week after the campaign broadcast slot began on Aug 28.

polls.note: AtlasIntel in partnership with Bloomberg, released on Aug 31 (UOL, Exame, Estadão, Poder360, Gazeta do Povo, VEJA, Brasil de Fato). [First round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) Lula 43.4% x Flávio Bolsonaro 33.7%, a distance of 9.7pp, with Augusto Cury at 7.8% and Renan Santos at 7.6% practically tied for third. [Runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) Lula 47.1% x Flávio 42.6%, a distance of 4.5pp. In the other runoff scenarios, Lula 46.6% x Ronaldo Caiado 41.0%, Lula 47.0% x Romeu Zema 40.7% and Lula 47.5% x Renan Santos 26.0%. The pollster also tested the scenario with Jair Bolsonaro, currently ineligible, in which Lula has 46.8% against 44.1%. Fieldwork Aug 25 to 30, n=5,014 surveyed by electronic form, margin of 1pp, 95% confidence, registration BR-07972/2026. It is the largest national sample in the panel's 30-day window. ⭐ ITS FIELDWORK CLOSED ON AUG 30, AFTER THE FREE ELECTORAL AIRTIME DEBUTED ON AUG 28, unlike Vox of Aug 29, whose fieldwork closed on Aug 27. The two are not comparable on that point. ⚠️ TWO NATIONAL POLLS CAME OUT ON THE SAME DAY AND DISAGREE ON THE SIZE OF THE GAP, not on its sign: this one gives 9.7pp in the first round and 4.5pp in the runoff, and BTG/Nexus of that same Aug 31 gives 6pp and 1pp. On the third-placed name the difference is 3.2pp, with 7.8% here and 11% there. Neither one contradicts the other about who is ahead.
polls.source: AtlasIntel in partnership with Bloomberg, released on Aug 31, 2026 (fieldwork Aug 25 to 30, n=5,014, electronic form, margin 1.0pp, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) registration BR-07972/2026). Figures checked against Gazeta do Povo, UOL, Exame, Estadão and Poder360.

polls.note: BTG/Nexus released on Aug 31 (CNN Brasil, UOL, Poder360, Gazeta do Povo, VEJA, CartaCapital) and also published on the pollster's own website. [First round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) Lula 39% x Flávio Bolsonaro 33%, a distance of 6pp, with Augusto Cury at 11%, Ronaldo Caiado at 5%, Renan Santos at 3% and Romeu Zema at 1%. [Runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) Lula 46% x Flávio 45%, inside the 2pp margin. Fieldwork Aug 28 to 30, n=2,005 by phone, margin of 2pp, 95% confidence, registration BR-08900/2026, commissioned by BTG Pactual. ⭐ THE COMPARISON THAT COUNTS IS WITH THE POLLSTER ITSELF, SAME METHOD AND SAME SAMPLE, AND IT SHOWS THE THIRD-PLACED NAME MULTIPLYING BY FIVE IN ONE WEEK: against Nexus of Aug 24, Cury goes from 2% to 11%, a gain of 9 points, the first name outside the top two to reach double digits in this series, according to CNN Brasil. Over the same interval the runner-up gives up 4 points, from 37% to 33%, and the leader gives up 2, from 41% to 39%. ⚠️ AND THE RUNOFF DID NOT MOVE: it was 46% to 45% on Aug 24 and it is still 46% to 45%, meaning the first-round rearrangement did not show up in the same pollster's runoff. 📌 Two national polls came out on this Aug 31 and they disagree on the size of the gap: this one gives 6pp in the first round and 1pp in the runoff, and AtlasIntel/Bloomberg of the same day gives 9.7pp and 4.5pp.
polls.source: BTG/Nexus, released on Aug 31, 2026 (fieldwork Aug 28 to 30, n=2,005, phone, margin 2.0pp, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) registration BR-08900/2026), commissioned by BTG Pactual. Figures checked against the pollster's website, CNN Brasil, UOL and Poder360.

polls.note: Vox Brasil national poll published Aug 29 (Metrópoles, CNN Brasil, VEJA, Exame, JOTA, Alagoas 24 Horas). First round Lula 37.1% x Flávio Bolsonaro 34.8%, a distance of 2.3pp, a technical tie by the 2.15pp margin; Ronaldo Caiado 5.0%, Renan Santos 3.3%, Romeu Zema 2.8%, Augusto Cury 2.6%, others 4.1%, blank and null 3.5% and don't know 6.8%. The table closes at 100.0. Runoff Flávio 45.1% x Lula 44.5%, also a technical tie. Fieldwork Aug 25 to 27, n=2,100, in person, margin 2.15pp, 95% confidence, registration BR-05519/2026, funded by the institute's own resources. ⭐ THE COMPARISON THAT COUNTS IS WITH THE POLLSTER ITSELF, SAME METHOD AND SAME SAMPLE, AND IT SHOWS THE RUNOFF FLIPPING IN ONE MONTH: on Jul 31 Vox measured first round Lula 40.5% x Flávio 31.2%, a distance of 9.3pp, and runoff Lula 47.5% x Flávio 41.1%, a distance of 6.4pp outside the margin. Now the first-round distance is 2.3pp and the runoff has changed sides, with 0.6pp for Flávio. That is 7.0 points of narrowing in the first round and 7.0 points of reversal in the runoff, which Exame also reported. ⚠️ THIS HOLDS FOR THE VOX SERIES, NOT FOR THE SET OF NATIONAL POLLS. Across the two Vox readings the sign of the runoff changed sides: on Jul 31 the leader was 6.4 points ahead and now he is 0.6 point behind. In the panel's 30-day window he had already appeared ahead in the runoff in three other national polls: Gerp of Aug 26, 47% to 42%, Veritá of Aug 21, 47.3% to 42%, and Gerp of Aug 11, 45% to 43%. The pollsters disagree with each other about the runoff, and the clearest case is Aug 26, when Gerp gave him 47% to 42% and Indexa/Broadcast gave the leader 46% to 41%, on the SAME day and with opposite signs. REJECTION of 52.7% for Lula and 49.3% for Flávio (CNN Brasil). Exame records disapproval of Lula at 53.3% in the same round. NATIONAL SCOPE confirmed on release. ⚠️ Fieldwork closed on Aug 27, BEFORE campaign advertising debuted on Aug 28, so this poll does not measure any advertising effect.
polls.source: Vox Brasil released on Aug 29 by Metrópoles, CNN Brasil, VEJA, Exame, JOTA and Alagoas 24 Horas. TSE registration BR-05519/2026.

polls.note: PoderData/Aya national poll released on Aug 27 (Poder360, Gazeta do Povo, CNN Brasil, Exame, UOL, CartaCapital, Jornal de Brasília, Pleno.News). First round Lula 38% x Flávio 35%, a distance of 3pp, a technical tie by the 2pp margin; Renan Santos, Ronaldo Caiado and Augusto Cury at 4% each, Pablo Marçal at 3% and Romeu Zema at 2%. Runoff Lula 45% x Flávio 44%, also a technical tie. Fieldwork Aug 23 to 26, n=2,400, telephone across 555 municipalities in the 27 federal units, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, registration BR-04974/2026. ⭐ THE COMPARISON THAT COUNTS IS WITH THE HOUSE ITSELF, AND IT SHOWS THE FIRST ROUND NARROWING BY HALF: it was 6pp on Jul 16 (40% x 34%), 6pp on Jul 30 (41% x 35%), 6pp on Aug 13 (41% x 35%) and it is 3pp now (38% x 35%). The runoff stays at 1pp, as on Aug 13. Same house, same method and same sample, with the first round narrowing and the runoff flat, the reverse of what the house’s series had been showing. REJECTION level at 49% for each of them (Poder360). The same round gives the leader a technical tie against Romeu Zema (44% x 43%) and against Ronaldo Caiado (44% x 43%), and a 7-point lead over Renan Santos (44% x 37%). ⭐ And Augusto Cury's 4% sits at the top of the range in which the panel's 11 readings measure him, from 1% to 4%. APPROVAL of the government at 42% against 50% disapproval, and the administration is rated poor or terrible by 48% against great or good by 33% (CNN Brasil). NATIONAL SCOPE confirmed in the release, which states 555 municipalities across the 27 federal units.
polls.source: PoderData/Aya, released on Aug 27 by Poder360, Gazeta do Povo, CNN Brasil, Exame, UOL Notícias, CartaCapital, Jornal de Brasília and Pleno.News. TSE registration BR-04974/2026.

polls.note: Gerp national poll released on Aug 26, registration BR-03547/2026, with 2,400 interviews and a 2pp margin at 95% confidence, costing R$ 20,000 from the firm's own funds. Checked against Poder360 and Gazeta do Povo, with the registration matching in both. ⭐ IT IS THE FIRST IN OUR TABLE IN WHICH FLÁVIO COMES OUT AHEAD IN THE FIRST ROUND, at 38% against Lula's 37%, inside the margin. The only other one in which he was not behind is Gerp's own poll of Aug 11, which showed a 38 to 38 tie. 📊 THE COMPARISON WITH THE HOUSE ITSELF: in the runoff the distance went from 2 points (Flávio 45 x Lula 43, registration BR-08045/2026, fieldwork Aug 6 to 10) to 5 points now, and in the first round Lula gave up 1 point in the same tracker. ⚠️ FILED IS NOT PUBLISHED, and here the two diverge: the TSE filing declares fieldwork from Aug 20 to 23 and publication expected on Aug 25, and the institute released it on Aug 26 reporting fieldwork from Aug 21 to 25. The table follows what the institute published, and the divergence is declared. 🔀 AND IT CAME OUT ON THE SAME DAY AS INDEXA, POINTING THE OTHER WAY: Gerp has Flávio winning the runoff by 5 and Indexa has Lula winning it by 5, with overlapping fieldwork windows. That is ten points apart between two houses on the same contest. 📌 The collection mode does not appear in the part of the filing I read, and the "Misto" label comes from the institute's profile, not from this round.
polls.source: Gerp, released on Aug 26, 2026 (fieldwork Aug 21 to 25 per the institute, n=2,400, 2.0pp margin, TSE registration BR-03547/2026, cost R$ 20,000 from its own funds). Figures checked against Poder360 and Gazeta do Povo, with registration BR-03547/2026 confirmed in both, and cross-checked against the Wikipedia table of 2026 presidential polls.

polls.note: Indexa/Broadcast national poll released on Aug 26, registration BR-06366/2026, with 2,000 individual telephone interviews and a 2.2pp margin at 95% confidence, costing R$ 164,000. Fieldwork Aug 20 to 23, and here the TSE filing and the release DO match. Checked against Gazeta do Povo, Money Times and CartaCapital, with the registration matching. 📊 COMPARISON WITH THE HOUSE ITSELF: its July round had Lula at 41% and Flávio at 31%, and it now has 39% and 34%, so the gap narrowed from 10 points to 5, with Lula giving up 2 and Flávio gaining 4. 📌 TWO FIRST-ROUND SCENARIOS, and the difference is Pablo Marçal: without him, Lula 39% and Flávio 34%; with him, Lula 39% and Flávio 33%, and Marçal comes in at 2%. Four runoff scenarios, all with Lula ahead: 46 x 41 against Flávio, 45 x 34 against Zema, 44 x 38 against Caiado and 46 x 34 against Renan Santos. 🔀 IT CAME OUT ON THE SAME DAY AS GERP, POINTING THE OTHER WAY: Indexa has Lula winning the runoff by 5 and Gerp has Flávio winning it by 5, with overlapping fieldwork windows. 🆕 The institute enters the table's roster today, with a reliability of 3 assigned by analogy with houses of similar standing, and that rating is editorial and open to revision.

polls.note: BTG/Nexus national poll released on Aug 24 at 6:36 AM, fieldwork Aug 21 to 23, registration BR-09028/2026, with 2,006 telephone interviews and a margin of 2pp at 95% confidence. Commissioned by BTG Pactual. Checked against Poder360, CNN Brasil, Metrópoles, Folha de S.Paulo, CartaCapital and Gazeta do Povo, with the registration number matching in all of them. ⭐ THE COMPARISON WITH THE HOUSE ITSELF IS THE FINDING, AND IT IS NOT A NEW LOW: in the first round the distance fell from 5 points to 4 and in the runoff from 3 to 1, but both values TIE the Aug 3 wave, which had already measured 41 to 37 and 46 to 45. The tracker's runoff series reads 4 points on Jul 27, 1 on Aug 3, 3 on Aug 10, 3 on Aug 17 and 1 now, meaning today's 1 point repeats a level the house had already recorded, and is not the narrowest of the series. 🕐 THE POLL DOES NOT MEASURE THE DEBATE: fieldwork closed on Aug 23 and the first presidential debate was at 8 PM that same day, on Band, without Lula and without Flávio Bolsonaro. Any headline linking one to the other falls outside the window. 📌 Two first-round scenarios, and the difference between them is Pablo Marçal: without him, Lula 41% and Flávio 37%; with him, Lula 40% and Flávio 34%, and Marçal appears with 4%. Runoff: Lula 46% x Flávio 45%, and Lula 46% x Ronaldo Caiado 42%, the latter according to Metrópoles. Rejection in the same wave, according to Poder360: Lula 49% and Flávio 48%. Evaluation of the administration in the same wave: 35% excellent or good and 43% poor or terrible, with 48% approval against 49% disapproval.

polls.note: Datafolha national poll released on Aug 21 at 6:30 PM, fieldwork Aug 18 to 20, TSE registration BR-04496/2026, 2,058 interviews with people aged 16 and over and a 2pp margin at 95% confidence. Commissioned by Globo and Folha de S.Paulo, it is the institute's first after the campaign began. ⭐ TWO SCENARIOS, and the difference between them is Marçal himself: with him, Flávio Bolsonaro has 32%; without him, 33%. Marçal comes in at 2%. Runoff: Lula 47% x Flávio Bolsonaro 43%, a distance at the edge of the margin. 🔴 THE FINDING OF THE DAY IS NOT IN THIS POLL, IT IS BETWEEN THIS ONE AND THE OTHER. The Veritá, released hours earlier with overlapping fieldwork (Aug 16 to 20), measured a 0.2 point TIE in the first round and gave the runoff INVERTED, with Flávio at 47.3% against 42%. That is more than 9 points of difference between two institutes on the same day, and the panel publishes both without choosing. ⚠️ Datafolha carries reliability 5 on this house's scale and Veritá carries 2. 📌 Rejection in the same round: Flávio 46% and Lula 45%. Government rating: 47% approve and 50% disapprove, against 49% and 48% in July. 72% say they are decided and 27% may still change.

polls.note: Veritá national poll released on Aug 21, fieldwork Aug 16 to 20, TSE registration BR-04006/2026, 3,840 interviews and a 2pp margin at 95% confidence. ⭐ STATISTICAL TIE IN THE FIRST ROUND: Lula 39.3% x Flávio Bolsonaro 39.1%, 0.2 point apart, against 5 points in the BTG/Nexus of Aug 17 (41% x 36%), whose fieldwork closed four days earlier. The two institutes are not measuring the same field: this round includes Pablo Marçal and the BTG/Nexus one does not. ⭐ IT WAS THE FIRST NATIONAL POLL RELEASED WITH PABLO MARÇAL IN THE FIELD, hours before the Datafolha of the same day, and he comes in at 5.2%, ahead of Renan Santos (3.8%) and Ronaldo Caiado (3.3%). 🔴 THE CROSSING WITH THE MARKET IS THE FINDING: the ballot gives Marçal 5.2% and the price pays 0.25% on him, confirmed reading of Aug 20 at 11:19 PM BRT, and that price sits below the 0.5% floor the capture guard watches. These are different quantities, voting intention and probability of winning, and they do not subtract; the panel records that the two order the field in opposite ways, without saying which one is right. Runoff: Flávio Bolsonaro 47.3% x Lula 42%. ⚠️ DECLARED PROVENANCE: the institute's own site had not published the round when the panel was updated, so the number does not come from the institute as primary source. It was checked against two independent readings, press coverage (CNN Brasil, Rádio Itatiaia and GP1) and the Wikipedia aggregator table, which record the same fieldwork, the same sample and the same percentages, and the first-round line adds up to 100.2% with undecideds, which is coherent. ⚠️ Rádio Itatiaia published the runoff as 47%, a rounding of 47.3%. ⚠️ Veritá carries reliability 2 on this house's scale, as always, and is not a reading to take on its own.
polls.source: Veritá, TSE registration BR-04006/2026, reported by CNN Brasil, Rádio Itatiaia and GP1 on Aug 21, and aggregated in the Wikipedia table. The institute's site had not published the round at the time of checking.

polls.note: BTG/Nexus national poll released on Aug 17, the 10th round of the house's series, checked against the pollster's own site (nexus.fsb.com.br) and reported by Folha de S.Paulo, UOL, Poder360, VEJA, CartaCapital, Metrópoles and Gazeta do Povo. Stimulated first round: Lula 41% x Flávio Bolsonaro 36%, with Ronaldo Caiado at 5%, Renan Santos at 4% and Romeu Zema at 4%. Runoff: Lula 47% x Flávio 44%. ⭐ THE COMPARISON WITH THE HOUSE'S OWN PREVIOUS ROUND IS THE DATA, AND IT IS ONE OF STABILITY: in the first round Lula went from 40% to 41% and Flávio from 35% to 36%, so the DISTANCE stayed at the same 5 points. In the runoff the result is IDENTICAL to the previous round, 47 to 44, keeping 3 points. Each 1-point move fits entirely inside the 2pp margin declared by the house. ⭐ THE PACK'S ORDERING IS INVERTED RELATIVE TO THE MARKET: Caiado appears at 5% and Renan Santos at 4%, while in the price Renan has 4.05% to win against Caiado's 0.25%. GOVERNMENT ASSESSMENT in the same round: 42% bad or terrible, 34% excellent or good and 23% average, according to Diário do Grande ABC, ndmais and A Folha das Cidades. ⛔ The panel does NOT publish the approve-and-disapprove pair from this round: outlets diverged between 47% against 48% (Metrópoles) and 46% against 49% (Brasil 247), and the pollster's own site did not carry the figure. Where the reading does not converge, the panel declares instead of choosing. ⚠️ The electoral court records the field as Aug 14 to 16 and the planned sample as 2,000; the pollster published 2,003 completed interviews.
polls.source: BTG/Nexus, checked at the primary source on nexus.fsb.com.br, and reported by Folha de S.Paulo, UOL, Poder360, VEJA, CartaCapital, Metrópoles and Gazeta do Povo, Aug 17

polls.note: Genial/Quaest national poll released Aug 14 at 9:00 pm (G1, CNN Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo, Valor Econômico, Estadão, Poder360, VEJA, InfoMoney, Correio Braziliense). First round Lula 38% x Flávio Bolsonaro 31%, a gap of 7pp, with Renan Santos and Ronaldo Caiado at 4% and Augusto Cury and Romeu Zema at 2%. Runoff Lula 43% x Flávio 40%, 3pp, with a margin of 2pp. ⭐ THE COMPARISON THAT COUNTS IS AGAINST THE HOUSE ITSELF, AND IT IS SYMMETRICAL: against the Quaest of Aug 5, the first round moved from 39% x 30% to 38% x 31% and the runoff moved from 44% x 39% to 43% x 40%. In both rounds Lula gave up 1 point and Flávio gained 1 point, and each gap narrowed by 2pp. Same house, same in-person method and same sample. REJECTION broken out for the first time in this window: Flávio 54%, Lula 52% and Caiado 35%, the last with high unfamiliarity declared by the house. GOVERNMENT ASSESSMENT: 46% approve and 48% disapprove; on the excellent/good, fair and poor/terrible scale, it is 36% positive, 25% fair and 37% negative, according to InfoMoney and UOL. ⭐ CROSSTABS RELEASED LATER, ON AUG 15 AND 16: how firm the vote is, with 77% of Lula's voters calling the decision final and 22% saying they could still change, and Zema's electorate emerging as the least convinced in the field, according to G1; and behaviour among independents, a segment where Flávio marks 35% against 29% for Lula in the runoff, according to O Globo. ⚠️ The electoral court records the field as Aug 10 to 13 and the house published Aug 10 to 12; the panel displays the registered period.
polls.source: Genial/Quaest via G1, CNN Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo, Valor Econômico, Estadão, Poder360, VEJA, InfoMoney, UOL and Correio Braziliense, Aug 14 to 16

polls.note: PoderData/Aya national poll published Aug 13 (Poder360, CNN Brasil, Exame, R7, Jovem Pan, Brasil 247, Gazeta do Povo). First round Lula 41% x Flávio 35%, a distance of 6pp. Runoff Lula 46% x Flávio 45%, 1pp, a statistical tie given the 2pp margin. Fieldwork Aug 9 to Aug 12, n=2,400, telephone, margin 2pp, 95% confidence, registration BR-06868/2026. ⭐ THE COMPARISON THAT COUNTS IS WITH THE HOUSE ITSELF, AND IT SEPARATES THE TWO ROUNDS: in the first round the gap did NOT move in four weeks, it was 6pp on Jul 16 (40% x 34%), 6pp on Jul 30 (41% x 35%) and it is 6pp now, with the top two repeating exactly the same values as the previous round; in the runoff the gap fell from 3pp to 1pp over the same span. Same house, same method and same sample, with the first round frozen and the runoff narrowing. REJECTION tied at 48% each (Poder360). CNN Brasil and Bnews record that Lula also ties with Zema and with Caiado in the runoff and beats Renan Santos; the percentages of those match-ups were not published in the articles captured and therefore do not appear here.
polls.source: PoderData/Aya published on Aug 13 by Poder360, CNN Brasil, Exame, R7, Jovem Pan, Brasil 247, Gazeta do Povo, Rádio Itatiaia and Portal Salvador FM. TSE registration BR-06868/2026.

polls.note: CNT/MDA national poll published Aug 11, commissioned by the National Transport Confederation. First round Lula 42.4% x Flávio 28.7%, a distance of 13.7pp. Runoff Lula 48% x Flávio 39%, 9pp. Field Aug 5 to 8, n=2,002, margin 2.2pp, 95% confidence, registration BR-06935/2026. ⚠️ IT IS THE MOST FAVOURABLE READING FOR THE LEADER AMONG THE SEVEN NATIONAL POLLS SINCE AUG 5, and on the same day Gerp published the least favourable one, with the challenger ahead in the runoff. The runner-up's 28.7% falls BELOW the floor the window held until yesterday, which was 30% at Genial/Quaest. GOVERNMENT RATING: 35% rate it excellent or good and 36% poor or terrible, practically tied.
polls.source: CNT/MDA released on Aug 11 by Estadão, UOL, Poder360, CartaCapital, VEJA, Gazeta do Povo, InfoMoney, O Povo and Revista Fórum. TSE registration BR-06935/2026.

polls.note: Gerp national poll published Aug 11. First round TIED at 38% x 38%, with Renan Santos 5%, Caiado 4%, Zema 2%, Cabo Daciolo and Augusto Cury 1% each, 7% undecided and 4% for none. Runoff Flávio 45% x Lula 43%. Field Aug 6 to 10, n=2,400, telephone, margin 2pp, 95% confidence, registration BR-08045/2026. ⚠️ IT IS THE FIRST NATIONAL POLL OF THE WINDOW TO PUT THE RUNNER-UP AHEAD IN THE RUNOFF, and the release itself treats the 2pp difference as a statistical tie within the margin. ON THE SAME DAY CNT/MDA published the leader 9pp ahead in the same scenario, which puts the two readings 11 points apart. GOVERNMENT DISAPPROVAL at 53%. 📌 The registration set publication for Aug 10 and it came out on Aug 11, which is a release delay, not fresh data.
polls.source: Gerp released on Aug 11 by Exame, Jovem Pan, Poder360, CNN Brasil and Gazeta do Povo. TSE registration BR-08045/2026.

polls.note: Futura Inteligência national poll published Aug 11. First round Lula 38.8% x Flávio 34.1%, a distance of 4.7pp. Runoff Lula 46.5% x Flávio 44%, 2.5pp, which the release treats as a statistical tie. Field Aug 3 to 7, n=2,000, telephone, margin 2.2pp, 95% confidence. REJECTION with Flávio at 47.1% and Lula at 45.9%, a statistical tie here too. GOVERNMENT APPROVAL at 47.3% against 49.9% disapproval. ⚠️ THE TSE REGISTRATION WAS NOT CLOSED WITH CERTAINTY: the window lists 100 Cidades with the same sample of n=2,000 and the same date, and the two brands publish together as 100% Cidades/Futura, but the match was not confirmed in a primary source. The panel declares the doubt instead of asserting the protocol. IT SITS IN THE MIDDLE OF TODAY'S THREE, between the leader's 9pp advantage at CNT/MDA and the challenger's 2pp at Gerp.
polls.source: Futura Inteligência released on Aug 11 by CNN Brasil, Exame, Gazeta do Povo, Jornal de Brasília, Brasil 247 and Jornal Opção. TSE registration not confirmed, see note.

polls.note: PALVER'S DEBUT on the panel, published Aug 10, with n=5,000, the largest sample among the national polls published in August. Over a 30-day window the AtlasIntel of Jul 29 was larger, with n=5,021. First round Lula 44% x Flávio 40%, with Renan Santos alone in third, on 10%. Runoff Lula 46% x Flávio 46%, a tie on the number. Margin 3pp, 95% confidence, register BR-06596/2026. THE TSE REGISTER DECLARES FIELDWORK FROM Aug 3 TO Aug 9 AND THE RELEASE REPORTS Aug 3 TO Aug 7, and the panel records both dates rather than picking one. THE METHOD POINT COMES FROM THE INSTITUTE ITSELF, not from this panel: Palver assessed that the digital format may have boosted Renan Santos' performance, since he keeps an active base in that environment, and said it is testing approaches to reduce that effect in online polls. With that, the same name appears at 4% and 4.7% in the telephone and in-person rounds of Aug 5, at 4% in today's telephone BTG/Nexus, and at 10% here, over the internet. REJECTION with Lula at 52% and Flávio at 51%. GOVERNMENT APPROVAL at 45% against 55% disapproval, the most negative balance among the houses of the window, in which the Genial/Quaest of Aug 5 marked 48% x 47% and today's BTG/Nexus marked 46% x 49%.
polls.source: Palver released on Aug 10 by Folha de S.Paulo, CNN Brasil, UOL, Exame, JOTA and CartaCapital. TSE register BR-06596/2026.

polls.note: BTG/Nexus national poll published Aug 10, the 9th round of the series. First round Lula 40% x Flávio 35%, with Caiado 5%, Renan Santos 4% and Zema 3%. The 5pp difference falls OUTSIDE the 2pp margin. Runoff Lula 47% x Flávio 44%, a 3pp difference that the release itself treats as a technical tie, and the round also points to Lula tying with Caiado in the runoff. Field Aug 7 to Aug 9, n=2,001, telephone, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, register BR-08428/2026. THE WITHIN-HOUSE COMPARISON REVERSES WHAT THE PREVIOUS ROUND SHOWED: on Aug 3 the first round gap had FALLEN from 9pp to 4pp, and now it has widened again, to 5pp. In the runoff the move is larger, from 1pp to 3pp. And both gave way in the first round, Lula from 41% to 40% and Flávio from 37% to 35%, which means the gap widened because the runner-up fell further, not because the leader rose. APPROVAL at 46% against 49% disapproval, against 47% x 48% in that house's own Aug 3 round. REJECTION with Flávio at 50% and Lula at 48%, and this time the figure came with a closed source, unlike the previous round, in which the secondary sources diverged and the panel left the number out.
polls.source: BTG/Nexus released on Aug 10 by Folha de S.Paulo, Estadão, Poder360, CNN Brasil, UOL, JOTA, CartaCapital, VEJA, Metrópoles, GZH, Money Times and Revista Fórum. TSE register BR-08428/2026.

polls.note: [Genial/Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) national poll published Aug 5 (G1, CNN Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo, Valor Econômico, O Globo, Estadão, VEJA, JOTA, Money Times, Poder360, Brasil de Fato). [First round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) Lula 39% x Flávio 30% (gap +9pp), with Caiado 4%, Renan Santos 4%, Zema 2%, Augusto Cury 1%, Cabo Daciolo 1%, Samara Martins 1%, blank and void 8%, undecided 10%. [Runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) Lula 44% x Flávio 39% (gap +5pp, blank and void 13%, undecided 4%); Lula 46% x Zema 34%; Lula 45% x Caiado 37%; Lula 45% x Renan Santos 35%. Lula wins all four runoff scenarios. REJECTION: 54% would not vote for Flávio and 41% would; 52% would not vote for Lula and 45% would. WITHIN-HOUSE COMPARISON, which is the only valid one: in the Jul 15 round it was 40% x 28%, a +12pp gap, and in the runoff 45% x 37%, a +8pp gap. So the first-round gap fell 3pp and the runoff gap fell 3pp, and the movement belongs to the challenger, who gains 2pp in the first round and 2pp in the runoff while Lula gives up 1pp in each. GOVERNMENT APPROVAL: 48% approve and 47% disapprove, with 5% no answer, numbers IDENTICAL to its own Jul 15 round. Administration ratings also repeat exactly: 36% positive, 26% average, 36% negative, 2% no answer. Two rounds by the same house with the same number on both indicators describe immobility, not a trend. Fieldwork Jul 31 to Aug 3, n=2,004, in person, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, commissioned by Banco Genial, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) registration BR-06591/2026.
polls.source: Genial/Quaest via G1, CNN Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo, Valor Econômico, O Globo, Estadão, JOTA, Money Times Aug 5

polls.note: Meio/Ideia (Instituto Ideia with Canal Meio) national poll published Aug 5 (Exame, Gazeta do Povo, JOTA, Estadão, Valor Econômico, Folha de S.Paulo, CartaCapital, Congresso em Foco). [First round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) Lula 43% x Flávio 35% (gap +8pp), with Caiado 5.7%, Renan Santos 4.7%, Zema 2.6%, Augusto Cury 1.7%, Cabo Daciolo 0.6%, Samara Martins 0.3%, Edmilson Costa 0.2%, Hertz Dias and Rui Costa Pimenta 0.1% each, blank and void 2%, don't know 4%. UNPROMPTED VOTE, which is a different question and does not mix with the prompted one: Lula 34.4%, Flávio 23%, undecided 27.7%. [Runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) Lula 48.5% x Flávio 43% (gap +5.5pp); Lula 48.5% x Zema 37%; Lula 48.5% x Caiado 40%; Lula 48% x Renan Santos 34.7%. Lula wins all four. WITHIN-HOUSE COMPARISON: in the Jul 8 round it was 40.4% x 32%, a +8.4pp gap, and in the runoff 45% x 40%, a +5pp gap. The first-round gap barely moved, from +8.4pp to +8pp, and neither did the runoff, from +5pp to +5.5pp. What rose were BOTH: Lula from 40.4% to 43% and Flávio from 32% to 35%, which describes vote concentrating on the top two rather than an advantage for either. Fieldwork Jul 31 to Aug 3, n=1,500, telephone, 2.5pp margin, 95% confidence, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) registration BR-04579/2026.
polls.source: Meio/Ideia via Exame, Gazeta do Povo, JOTA, Estadão, Valor Econômico, Folha de S.Paulo Aug 5

polls.note: [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) national poll released Aug 3, the 8th round in the series, and the first of the four national polls the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) filing had scheduled between Aug 3 and Aug 5. First round Lula 41% x Flávio 37%, with Caiado at 5%, Renan Santos at 4% and Zema at 3%. Runoff Lula 46% x Flávio 45%, a 1pp difference that falls WITHIN the 2pp margin and is therefore a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico). Fieldwork Jul 31 to Aug 2, n=2,002, telephone, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, filing BR-02874/2026. WHAT CHANGES THE WEEK IS THE COMPARISON WITH THE INSTITUTE'S OWN PREVIOUS ROUND: the first-round gap FELL FROM 9pp TO 4pp in a single round, against the 42% x 33% of Jul 27. And the move comes almost entirely from one side, because LULA GAVE UP 1pp and FLÁVIO GAINED 4pp. In the runoff the tightening is sharper still, from 4pp to 1pp, with Lula going from 47% to 46% and Flávio from 43% to 45%. The round's other runoffs: Lula 46% x Caiado 42%, Lula 46% x Zema 40% and Lula 47% x Renan Santos 37%. AGAINST THE OTHER HOUSES, among the four national polls released since Jul 29 this is the one showing the tightest first round: 4pp here, against 6pp in PoderData of Jul 30, 9.1pp in [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29 and 9.3pp in Vox Brasil of Jul 31. The distance between the highest and the lowest reading reaches 5.3pp and is larger than any price move in the period. ⚠️ REJECTION NOT PUBLISHED BY THIS PANEL: the secondary sources DISAGREE. Poder360, CNN Brasil and Correio Braziliense report 49% for each of the two; Money Times reports 50% for Lula and 51% for Flávio. The institute's release note does not carry the figure, so it could not be settled against a primary source and the number stays out, with the disagreement declared here. ⚠️ CORRECTION PUBLISHED ON Aug 4: this entry said the round had carried no approval figures, and it had. The data came out in the Aug 4 coverage, from the SAME round BR-02874/2026: government approval at 47% against 48% disapproval, and administration ratings at 37% excellent or good, 18% average and 43% poor or terrible. The panel corrects rather than rewriting in silence.
polls.source: BTG/Nexus via the institute's own site (nexus.fsb.com.br), Folha de S.Paulo, Estadão, CNN Brasil, JOTA, CartaCapital, Poder360, VEJA, Exame, Correio Braziliense and Money Times Aug 3. TSE filing BR-02874/2026.

approvalData.note: 🏷️ THE STRUCTURED FIGURES IN THIS BLOCK COME FROM GENIAL/QUAEST OF AUG 14, and they are: 46% approval against 48% disapproval, with 6% don't know, and 36% excellent or good, 25% fair and 37% poor or terrible. The panel keeps ONE pollster per block on purpose, so as not to add up the rulers of different houses. ⭐ TWO NEW READINGS ON AUG 31, declared here and NOT mixed into the figures above, both with fieldwork closed on Aug 30, that is, already after the free electoral airtime debuted on Aug 28. BTG/Nexus brings 46% approval against 51% disapproval (Poder360), and the pollster itself records that the distance between the two is the widest since May (VEJA). AtlasIntel/Bloomberg brings disapproval at 52.9%, with the rise concentrated among younger voters and lower income brackets (InfoMoney). 📌 REJECTION of the top two names, also in the two Aug 31 rounds: AtlasIntel gives 52.7% for the runner-up and 52.0% for the leader (CNN Brasil, UOL), and BTG/Nexus gives 50% for the runner-up and 49% for the leader (Metrópoles). In both houses the runner-up is the more rejected of the two, and in both the difference between them fits inside the margin. 📌 The earlier readings of the week still hold as series: PoderData/Aya of Aug 27 with 42% against 50%, Indexa/Broadcast of Aug 26 with 46% against 50% and Gerp of Aug 26 with 43% against 51%. ⚠️ Each house uses its own approval ruler, so the comparison that counts is each pollster against itself, never one pollster against another.
approvalData.source: Approval and disapproval: Genial/Quaest Aug 14, 2026 (fieldwork Aug 10 to Aug 13, n=2,004, in person across 120 municipalities, margin 2.0pp, TSE registration BR-06773/2026), released by G1, CNN Brasil, Estadão, Correio Braziliense and Poder360. Rejection: same round, via G1, Poder360, InfoMoney and O Globo. Government-performance breakdown (very good/good, average, bad/very bad): Genial/Quaest Aug 5, 2026, because the Aug 14 round did not carry that breakdown in the reports captured.

polymarketComparison.note: Polymarket prices in the confirmed reading of Sep 1, 8:34 PM BRT (11:34 PM UTC), with the presidential book at USD 141.39M. ONE NATIONAL POLL WAS RELEASED THIS TUESDAY, Real Time Big Data (BR-03490/2026, field Aug 27 to 31, n=2,000, margin of 2pp), and it is the first in the panel whose field reaches Aug 31, that is, the first to cover the full week after the campaign broadcast slot began on Aug 28. ⚠️ THE POLLSTER PUBLISHED TWO FIRST-ROUND SCENARIOS: with Pablo Marçal on the list, 38% to 29% with Augusto Cury at 10%; without Marçal, 38% to 30% with Cury at 11%. The day’s headlines circulated the second without saying which one it was. In the runoff, the leader and the runner-up went back to a tie, at 44% to 44%. ⭐ AND IN THE SCENARIO AGAINST RONALDO CAIADO THE LEADER COMES OUT BEHIND, 45% TO 43%: across the 41 runoff simulations in the panel’s base he has trailed in four, and all four were against the runner-up, so it is the first time a name other than him shows in front. In the price, the leader has not left 55.50% for the fourth day running and the runner-up gave up 0.10pp, to 38.95%, so the distance widened from 16.45pp to 16.55pp. What moved were the names below: Renan Santos rose 0.70pp, to 2.55%, and Augusto Cury rose 0.50pp, to 2.35%. The two quantities do not subtract: the poll measures declared voting intention, including in hypothetical scenarios, and the price measures the chance of winning the real election.
polymarketComparison.sources: Polymarket prices via the AFOS proxy, and the panel only publishes a price that two independent readings, taken eight minutes apart, confirm within 0.20pp. The confirmation is done contract by contract. On Aug 27 all five books tracked confirmed in the 10:49 PM reading, including Augusto Cury's contract, which opened that same day. Polls filed with the TSE and released by the institutes, as reported by Poder360, Gazeta do Povo, CNN Brasil, Exame, UOL, CartaCapital, G1, Folha de S.Paulo, O Globo, Estadão, Valor Econômico, VEJA, BBC and Jornal de Brasília. PoderData/Aya of Aug 27 was checked against two sources, with the TSE registration number matching and with the national scope confirmed in the release, which states 555 municipalities across the 27 federal units. Series superlatives checked in the Neon backup, in backup/neon/marketPrice, which holds the full record since Apr 14.
